title: Carolina Mustard Pulled Pork
seoTitle: Carolina Mustard Pulled Pork | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Tangy mustard pull, soft buns
description: Tangy mustard pull, soft buns. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large covered roaster or slow cooker

steps.title: Season the shoulder
steps.instruction: Mix salt, pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder; rub all over pork shoulder. Let sit 30 minutes while the oven or slow cooker heats — this is pulled pork, not grilled chops.

steps.title: Low-and-slow until shreddable
steps.instruction: Cook covered at 275°F or slow-cooker on low 8–10 hours until pork probes tender at 203°F. Add a splash of vinegar if the pan looks dry.

steps.title: Shred and finish with mustard sauce
steps.instruction: Rest pork 20 minutes, then shred. Whisk mustard, vinegar, brown sugar, and hot sauce; toss pork with enough sauce to coat — Carolina mustard pull should taste tangy, not like soy glaze.

steps.title: Quick slaw and warm buns
steps.instruction: Toss coleslaw with mayo and a spoon of mustard sauce. Warm buns wrapped in foil at 300°F.

steps.title: Build mustard pulled pork sandwiches
steps.instruction: Pile pork on buns with slaw and pickles. Keep extra mustard sauce for the line — this is Carolina Mustard Pulled Pork, not grilled tenderloin slices.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Rest grilled proteins 5–8 minutes under foil before slicing — juices stay in the meat.
tonightSpread: Plate Carolina Mustard Pulled Pork with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Carolina Mustard Pulled Pork on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
Slice proteins on a cutting board at the end of the line so everyone sees the smoke ring and char.
Set sauce and pickles on the side — sauced meat holds better on the backup tray.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tangy mustard pull, soft buns. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
